1	# makecar — MakeHuman for cars
2	
3	![the eight body styles](docs/images/lineup_styles.png)
4	
5	`makecar` procedurally models complete cars — exterior **and** interior — from a
6	config file, using the same ideas that make [MakeHuman](http://www.makehumancommunity.org/)
7	work for people:
8	
9	| MakeHuman                         | makecar                                                     |
10	|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
11	| one base mesh, fixed topology     | one parametric body loft with fixed topology (`body/generator.py`) |
12	| targets = per-vertex offsets      | `Target` objects, differential + sculpted (`morph/`, `body/targets.py`) |
13	| modifiers / sliders in [-1, 1]    | `Modifier`s: 39 shape sliders, 4 sculpts, 7 style macros    |
14	| macro targets (gender, age …)     | style macros: hatchback, wagon, suv, pickup, coupe, sports, van |
15	| joints / landmarks follow the mesh| **connectors** derived from vertex groups of the morphed mesh |
16	| proxies / clothes fitted to body  | **components** fitted to connectors, themselves target-based |
17	
18	```
19	config.yaml ──► CarBody (base + targets) ──► body mesh + connectors
20	                                                  │
21	                     components (wheel, seat, dashboard …) fitted to connectors
22	                     (components can emit connectors of their own → recursive)
23	                                                  │
24	                    output/<name>/  car.obj  body.obj  connectors.json  assembly.json
25	                                    blueprint.svg  connector_map.svg  preview.png  interior.png  spec.txt
26	```
27	
28	![sedan hero](docs/images/hero_family_sedan.png)
29	![sedan interior](docs/images/interior_family_sedan.png)
30	![slider sweeps](docs/images/slider_sweeps.png)
31	
32	## Quick start
33	
34	```bash
35	pip install numpy pyyaml            # the only runtime dependencies
36	python -m makecar samples -o output # builds every config in configs/ (the shipped samples)
37	python -m makecar build configs/coupe.yaml -o output --set wheelbase=0.4 --seed 3
38	python -m makecar list-modifiers    # all sliders with their groups and ranges
39	python -m makecar list-components   # registered components, what they accept, what they default for
40	python -m makecar connectors configs/suv.yaml   # every connector a config produces and what attaches
41	python -m makecar random -n 4 --style hatchback -o output   # random variations
42	python -m pytest -q                 # test-suite
43	```
44	
45	The first run builds the body target library (~4 s) and caches it in
46	`~/.cache/makecar/` (override with `MAKECAR_CACHE`); afterwards a car builds in
47	well under a second, plus a few seconds for the PNG previews (pure-numpy
48	rasteriser — no renderer dependency).
49	
50	## Config file
51	
52	```yaml
53	name: gt_coupe
54	description: Two-door GT with muscular haunches
55	seed: 6
56	body:
57	  style: coupe                    # a macro target, or a blend: {suv: 0.7, coupe: 0.3}
58	  modifiers:                      # MakeHuman-style sliders in [-1, 1]
59	    cowl_offset: 0.3              #   long hood
60	    roof_height: -0.15
61	    width: 0.2
62	  sculpt: {haunches: 0.8, wedge: 0.5}   # hand-authored procedural targets
63	  hints: {door_count: 2, drive: left, transmission: manual, seat_rows: auto, fuel_side: left}
64	  random: {amount: 0.0}           # jitter the sliders for variations (uses `seed`)
65	palette: {paint: "#151820", interior: "#3a1f1c", seat: "#6b2f28", rim: "#d0d3d8"}
66	components:
67	  defaults: true                  # attach the default component to every connector
68	  disable: [antenna, roof_rail*]  # selectors: connector name, tag or glob
69	  assign:                         # override component and/or options per selector
70	    wheel: {component: wheel.alloy, options: {spokes: 10, spoke_width: 0.4}}
71	    exhaust: {component: exhaust.tip, options: {dual: true}}
72	    roof_rail: roof.rails         # opt-in component for a connector with no default
73	output:
74	  formats: [obj, svg, png, json]  # add "targets" to also dump the used targets as .target files
75	  views: [three_quarter_front, three_quarter_rear, side, top, front, rear, interior_cutaway, interior_side, driver]
76	  blueprint_theme: blueprint      # or "paper"; blueprint_connectors: true overlays every connector on the sheet
77	variants:                         # more cars from the same file (deep-merged over the base config)
78	  - name: gt_coupe_wide
79	    body: {modifiers: {width: 0.8}}
80	```
81	
82	`body.base_params` (advanced) regenerates the *base* mesh with different
83	canonical parameters; targets are still applied on top, exactly like editing the
84	MakeHuman base mesh.
85	
86	## The body: a fixed-topology loft with targets
87	
88	`body/generator.py` lofts 45 cross-section rings (64 vertices each) plus two
89	fascia caps. Every ring is sampled from ten *semantic* control points —
90	floor edge, wheel-well, sill, belt line, shoulder, roof rail, roof centre … —
91	with a fixed number of samples per segment, so vertex *j* of every ring is
92	always the same feature (sill, glass base, roof rail …) no matter what the
93	parameters are. Two independent chains of longitudinal breakpoints (wheel arches
94	vs. greenhouse features) share the ring index, which lets both wheel arches and
95	window apertures have clean edges without ever changing topology.
96	
97	Because the topology is fixed, `body/targets.py` derives targets exactly the way
98	MakeHuman targets were made: generate a variant, subtract the base.
99	
100	* 39 **differential modifiers** (`wheelbase`, `roof_height`, `windshield_length`,
101	  `a_pillar_lean`, `bed_depth`, …) each with a `-incr`/`-decr` target pair.
102	* 7 **style macros** (`style/hatchback` … `style/van`) — full presets turned into
103	  unipolar targets; they blend (`{sedan: 0.5, wagon: 0.5}` is a shooting brake).
104	* 4 **sculpt targets** written as displacement fields (`sculpt/haunches`,
105	  `sculpt/side_crease`, `sculpt/wedge`, `sculpt/roof_bubble`).
106	
107	The body mesh carries *zones* (apertures for glass and lamps, underbody, wheel
108	wells, bed) and *vertex groups* (arch lips, feature lines, rings at the cowl /
109	pillars / deck, nose & tail). Apertures are cut out of the shell and handed to
110	components as polygon connectors.
111	
112	## Connectors
113	
114	`connectors.py`:
115	
116	```
117	Connector
118	 ├── PointConnector                  mirrors, handles, badges, antenna, shifter, grab handles …
119	 └── PolygonConnector                windows, lamps, dashboard, headliner, door cards
120	      ├── RectangleConnector         seats, grille, plates, console, floor, pedals, cluster, screen …
121	      └── CircleConnector            wheels, steering wheel, exhaust, fuel cap, vents, speakers, cup holders
122	```
123	
124	Each connector has a `Frame` (origin + axes; Z = mount normal, X = major
125	direction), `tags` used by the config selectors, and `meta` hints (tyre width,
126	H-point height, driver side, grid shape of an aperture …). The body emits ~50 of
127	them, all computed from vertex groups and measurements of the *morphed* mesh, so
128	they follow every slider. Components can emit sub-connectors (the dashboard
129	offers a gauge cluster, screen, vents, glove box, HVAC; the console offers a
130	shifter and cup holders; door cards offer speakers …) and the assembler resolves
131	them recursively.
132	
133	Type matching uses the class hierarchy: a component that `accepts =
134	(PolygonConnector,)` attaches to rectangles and circles too.
135	
136	## Components
137	
138	`components/base.py` defines two flavours:
139	
140	* `CarComponent` — plain procedural (grille, plates, lamps, mirrors, …).
141	* `MorphableComponent` — **the same logic as the body**: a dataclass of canonical
142	  parameters, a fixed-topology `generate()`, a list of `ModifierSpec`s turned into
143	  differential targets by `DifferentialTargetBuilder`, optional variant macros,
144	  and a `fit()` that maps the connector's geometry (radius, width, height,
145	  meta) onto slider values. `Wheel`, the seats, the dashboard and the steering
146	  wheel work this way, so a wheel connector with a bigger radius simply drives
147	  the `radius` slider of the wheel library.
148	
149	Polygon-type components use `components/fills.py`: apertures come with the
150	grid shape of the loft region they were cut from, so a Coons patch reproduces the
151	body's curvature exactly (windshields stay double-curved; lamps wrap the corner).
152	
153	Register your own with `@register` and set `default_for` to the tags it should
154	take over by default, or select it explicitly in the config.
155	
156	## Output folder
157	
158	Each car gets `output/<name>/` with:
159	
160	* `car.obj` + `car.mtl` — full assembly (object groups per component, materials)
161	* `body.obj` — the morphed shell alone, apertures removed
162	* `connectors.json` — every connector: kind, frame, outline/size, tags, meta, attached component
163	* `assembly.json` — effective modifier values, measurements, component tree, timings
164	* `blueprint.svg` — A3 general-arrangement sheet: side/front/plan/rear views with mm dimensions, interior plan and centre-plane section, title block
165	* `connector_map.svg` — side + plan views with every connector drawn and labelled (colour-coded by kind)
166	* `preview.png`, `interior.png` — rendered views (roof cutaway, half-cut, driver's eye)
167	* `spec.txt` — human-readable summary
168	
169	`output/README.md` (written by `samples`) indexes all generated cars.
170	
171	## Layout
172	
173	```
174	makecar/
175	  geometry/    mesh container, frames, curves, primitives
176	  morph/       Target, Modifier, MorphableMesh, DifferentialTargetBuilder
177	  body/        params, generator (loft), styles (macros), targets, connectors, CarBody
178	  components/  base API + fills, exterior.py, interior.py
179	  export/      obj, svg blueprint, png rasteriser
180	  connectors.py  assembly.py  config.py  pipeline.py  cli.py
181	configs/       sample configs        tests/   pytest suite
182	```

1	"""Polygon mesh container with materials, vertex groups and face zones.
2	
3	Faces are stored as a list of index tuples (quads and triangles mixed) so that
4	the loft topology stays readable; `triangulated()` gives an (M,3) array for
5	rendering.  Vertex *groups* (named vertex index sets) are the MakeHuman analogue
6	of landmark/joint vertex groups: connectors are derived from them so that they
7	follow the mesh when targets are applied.  Face *zones* are named face index
8	sets used for materials and for apertures (windows, lights) that are removed
9	from the body and handed to components as polygon connectors.
10	"""
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
14	from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple
15	import numpy as np
16	
17	
18	@dataclass
19	class Material:
20	    name: str
21	    color: Tuple[float, float, float] = (0.7, 0.7, 0.7)
22	    alpha: float = 1.0
23	    shininess: float = 0.3
24	    emissive: float = 0.0
25	    metallic: float = 0.0
26	
27	    @staticmethod
28	    def parse_color(c) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
29	        if isinstance(c, str):
30	            s = c.lstrip("#")
31	            if len(s) == 3:
32	                s = "".join(ch * 2 for ch in s)
33	            return tuple(int(s[i : i + 2], 16) / 255.0 for i in (0, 2, 4))  # type: ignore
34	        c = tuple(float(v) for v in c)
35	        if max(c) > 1.0:
36	            c = tuple(v / 255.0 for v in c)
37	        return c  # type: ignore
38	
39	    def with_color(self, c, name: Optional[str] = None) -> "Material":
40	        m = Material(name or self.name, Material.parse_color(c), self.alpha, self.shininess, self.emissive, self.metallic)
41	        return m
42	
43	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
44	        return {
45	            "name": self.name,
46	            "color": [round(v, 4) for v in self.color],
47	            "alpha": self.alpha,
48	            "shininess": self.shininess,
49	            "emissive": self.emissive,
50	            "metallic": self.metallic,
51	        }
52	
53	
54	DEFAULT_MATERIAL = Material("default")
55	
56	
57	class Mesh:
58	    def __init__(
59	        self,
60	        vertices=None,
61	        faces: Optional[Sequence[Sequence[int]]] = None,
62	        face_materials: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
63	        materials: Optional[Dict[str, Material]] = None,
64	        name: str = "mesh",
65	    ):
66	        self.name = name
67	        self.vertices = np.zeros((0, 3)) if vertices is None else np.asarray(vertices, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 3)
68	        self.faces: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = [tuple(int(i) for i in f) for f in (faces or [])]
69	        if face_materials is None:
70	            face_materials = [DEFAULT_MATERIAL.name] * len(self.faces)
71	        self.face_materials: List[str] = list(face_materials)
72	        self.materials: Dict[str, Material] = dict(materials or {})
73	        if DEFAULT_MATERIAL.name not in self.materials and DEFAULT_MATERIAL.name in self.face_materials:
74	            self.materials[DEFAULT_MATERIAL.name] = DEFAULT_MATERIAL
75	        self.groups: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
76	        self.zones: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
77	        self.lines: List[np.ndarray] = []  # decorative polylines (seams etc.), world coords (K,3)
78	        self.line_names: List[str] = []
79	        self.meta: Dict[str, Any] = {}     # generator bookkeeping (copied, not exported)
80	
81	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- basics
82	    @property
83	    def n_vertices(self) -> int:
84	        return len(self.vertices)
85	
86	    @property
87	    def n_faces(self) -> int:
88	        return len(self.faces)
89	
90	    def copy(self) -> "Mesh":
91	        m = Mesh(self.vertices.copy(), list(self.faces), list(self.face_materials), dict(self.materials), self.name)
92	        m.groups = {k: v.copy() for k, v in self.groups.items()}
93	        m.zones = {k: v.copy() for k, v in self.zones.items()}
94	        m.lines = [l.copy() for l in self.lines]
95	        m.line_names = list(self.line_names)
96	        m.meta = dict(self.meta)
97	        return m
98	
99	    def bounds(self) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
100	        if self.n_vertices == 0:
101	            return np.zeros(3), np.zeros(3)
102	        return self.vertices.min(axis=0), self.vertices.max(axis=0)
103	
104	    def add_material(self, mat: Material) -> Material:
105	        self.materials[mat.name] = mat
106	        return mat
107	
108	    def set_material(self, name: str, face_indices=None):
109	        if face_indices is None:
110	            self.face_materials = [name] * self.n_faces
111	        else:
112	            for i in np.asarray(face_indices).ravel():
113	                self.face_materials[int(i)] = name
114	
115	    def add_group(self, name: str, indices: Iterable[int]):
116	        self.groups[name] = np.asarray(list(indices), dtype=int)
117	
118	    def add_zone(self, name: str, face_indices: Iterable[int]):
119	        self.zones[name] = np.asarray(list(face_indices), dtype=int)
120	
121	    def add_line(self, pts, name: str = "line"):
122	        self.lines.append(np.asarray(pts, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 3))
123	        self.line_names.append(name)
124	
125	    # ---------------------------------------------------------- transforms
126	    def transform(self, m4: np.ndarray) -> "Mesh":
127	        r, t = m4[:3, :3], m4[:3, 3]
128	        self.vertices = self.vertices @ r.T + t
129	        self.lines = [l @ r.T + t for l in self.lines]
130	        if np.linalg.det(r) < 0:
131	            self.faces = [tuple(reversed(f)) for f in self.faces]
132	        return self
133	
134	    def translate(self, d) -> "Mesh":
135	        d = np.asarray(d, dtype=float)
136	        self.vertices = self.vertices + d
137	        self.lines = [l + d for l in self.lines]
138	        return self
139	
140	    def scale(self, s) -> "Mesh":
141	        s = np.asarray(s, dtype=float)
142	        self.vertices = self.vertices * s
143	        self.lines = [l * s for l in self.lines]
144	        if np.ndim(s) and np.prod(np.sign(s)) < 0:
145	            self.faces = [tuple(reversed(f)) for f in self.faces]
146	        return self
147	
148	    def apply_frame(self, frame) -> "Mesh":
149	        """Interpret current coordinates as local to `frame` and map to world."""
150	        return self.transform(frame.matrix)
151	
152	    def mirrored(self, axis: int = 1) -> "Mesh":
153	        s = np.ones(3)
154	        s[axis] = -1.0
155	        m = self.copy()
156	        m.scale(s)
157	        return m
158	
159	    # ---------------------------------------------------------- topology
160	    def merge(self, other: "Mesh", group_prefix: Optional[str] = None) -> "Mesh":
161	        off = self.n_vertices
162	        foff = self.n_faces
163	        self.vertices = np.vstack([self.vertices, other.vertices]) if self.n_vertices else other.vertices.copy()
164	        self.faces.extend(tuple(i + off for i in f) for f in other.faces)
165	        self.face_materials.extend(other.face_materials)
166	        for k, v in other.materials.items():
167	            self.materials.setdefault(k, v)
168	        for k, v in other.groups.items():
169	            key = f"{group_prefix}/{k}" if group_prefix else k
170	            self.groups[key] = v + off
171	        for k, v in other.zones.items():
172	            key = f"{group_prefix}/{k}" if group_prefix else k
173	            self.zones[key] = v + foff
174	        self.lines.extend(l.copy() for l in other.lines)
175	        self.line_names.extend(other.line_names)
176	        return self
177	
178	    def remove_faces(self, face_indices) -> "Mesh":
179	        drop = set(int(i) for i in np.asarray(face_indices).ravel())
180	        if not drop:
181	            return self
182	        keep = [i for i in range(self.n_faces) if i not in drop]
183	        remap = {old: new for new, old in enumerate(keep)}
184	        self.faces = [self.faces[i] for i in keep]
185	        self.face_materials = [self.face_materials[i] for i in keep]
186	        new_zones = {}
187	        for k, v in self.zones.items():
188	            nv = np.asarray([remap[i] for i in v if i in remap], dtype=int)
189	            if len(nv):
190	                new_zones[k] = nv
191	        self.zones = new_zones
192	        return self
193	
194	    def prune_unused_vertices(self) -> "Mesh":
195	        used = np.zeros(self.n_vertices, dtype=bool)
196	        for f in self.faces:
197	            used[list(f)] = True
198	        if used.all():
199	            return self
200	        remap = -np.ones(self.n_vertices, dtype=int)
201	        remap[used] = np.arange(used.sum())
202	        self.vertices = self.vertices[used]
203	        self.faces = [tuple(int(remap[i]) for i in f) for f in self.faces]
204	        self.groups = {k: remap[v][remap[v] >= 0] for k, v in self.groups.items()}
205	        return self
206	
207	    def triangulated(self) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
208	        """Return (tris (M,3) int, tri_face_index (M,) int) using fan triangulation."""
209	        tris, owner = [], []
210	        for fi, f in enumerate(self.faces):
211	            for k in range(1, len(f) - 1):
212	                tris.append((f[0], f[k], f[k + 1]))
213	                owner.append(fi)
214	        if not tris:
215	            return np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=int), np.zeros(0, dtype=int)
216	        return np.asarray(tris, dtype=int), np.asarray(owner, dtype=int)
217	
218	    def _faces_by_size(self):
219	        groups: Dict[int, List[int]] = {}
220	        for i, f in enumerate(self.faces):
221	            groups.setdefault(len(f), []).append(i)
222	        return groups
223	
224	    def face_normals(self) -> np.ndarray:
225	        """Unit normals per face (Newell's method, vectorised per polygon size)."""
226	        n = np.zeros((self.n_faces, 3))
227	        v = self.vertices
228	        for size, idx in self._faces_by_size().items():
229	            idx = np.asarray(idx)
230	            F = np.asarray([self.faces[i] for i in idx], dtype=int)  # (m, size)
231	            P = v[F]                                                 # (m, size, 3)
232	            Q = np.roll(P, -1, axis=1)
233	            nx = np.sum((P[:, :, 1] - Q[:, :, 1]) * (P[:, :, 2] + Q[:, :, 2]), axis=1)
234	            ny = np.sum((P[:, :, 2] - Q[:, :, 2]) * (P[:, :, 0] + Q[:, :, 0]), axis=1)
235	            nz = np.sum((P[:, :, 0] - Q[:, :, 0]) * (P[:, :, 1] + Q[:, :, 1]), axis=1)
236	            nn = np.column_stack([nx, ny, nz])
237	            l = np.linalg.norm(nn, axis=1, keepdims=True)
238	            n[idx] = nn / np.maximum(l, 1e-12)
239	        return n
240	
241	    def face_centroids(self) -> np.ndarray:
242	        c = np.zeros((self.n_faces, 3))
243	        v = self.vertices
244	        for size, idx in self._faces_by_size().items():
245	            idx = np.asarray(idx)
246	            F = np.asarray([self.faces[i] for i in idx], dtype=int)
247	            c[idx] = v[F].mean(axis=1)
248	        return c
249	
250	    def vertex_normals(self) -> np.ndarray:
251	        fn = self.face_normals()
252	        vn = np.zeros_like(self.vertices)
253	        for f, n in zip(self.faces, fn):
254	            vn[list(f)] += n
255	        l = np.linalg.norm(vn, axis=1, keepdims=True)
256	        return vn / np.maximum(l, 1e-12)
257	
258	    def flip_normals(self) -> "Mesh":
259	        self.faces = [tuple(reversed(f)) for f in self.faces]
260	        return self
261	
262	    def boundary_loops(self, face_indices=None) -> List[List[int]]:
263	        """Ordered vertex loops bounding the given faces (default: whole mesh)."""
264	        faces = self.faces if face_indices is None else [self.faces[i] for i in np.asarray(face_indices).ravel()]
265	        edge_count: Dict[Tuple[int, int], int] = {}
266	        directed: Dict[Tuple[int, int], int] = {}
267	        for f in faces:
268	            for a, b in zip(f, f[1:] + f[:1]):
269	                key = (min(a, b), max(a, b))
270	                edge_count[key] = edge_count.get(key, 0) + 1
271	                directed[(a, b)] = directed.get((a, b), 0) + 1
272	        boundary = [(a, b) for (a, b) in directed if edge_count[(min(a, b), max(a, b))] == 1]
273	        nxt: Dict[int, List[int]] = {}
274	        for a, b in boundary:
275	            nxt.setdefault(a, []).append(b)
276	        loops = []
277	        used = set()
278	        for a, b in boundary:
279	            if (a, b) in used:
280	                continue
281	            loop = [a]
282	            cur, prev = b, a
283	            used.add((a, b))
284	            guard = 0
285	            while cur != a and guard < 100000:
286	                loop.append(cur)
287	                cands = [c for c in nxt.get(cur, []) if (cur, c) not in used]
288	                if not cands:
289	                    break
290	                c = cands[0]
291	                used.add((cur, c))
292	                prev, cur = cur, c
293	                guard += 1
294	            loops.append(loop)
295	        return loops
296	
297	    def zone_faces(self, name: str) -> np.ndarray:
298	        return self.zones.get(name, np.zeros(0, dtype=int))
299	
300	    def subset(self, face_indices) -> "Mesh":
301	        idx = np.asarray(face_indices, dtype=int).ravel()
302	        m = Mesh(self.vertices.copy(), [self.faces[i] for i in idx], [self.face_materials[i] for i in idx], dict(self.materials), self.name)
303	        m.prune_unused_vertices()
304	        return m
305	
306	    def stats(self) -> dict:
307	        lo, hi = self.bounds()
308	        return {
309	            "vertices": int(self.n_vertices),
310	            "faces": int(self.n_faces),
311	            "bounds_min": [round(float(v), 4) for v in lo],
312	            "bounds_max": [round(float(v), 4) for v in hi],
313	            "materials": sorted(self.materials.keys()),
314	        }
315	
316	    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover
317	        return f"Mesh({self.name!r}, {self.n_vertices} verts, {self.n_faces} faces)"

1	"""Derive measurements, feature lines (seams) and connectors from a morphed body.
2	
3	Everything here reads *vertex groups* and the aperture grid recorded by the
4	generator, never the generator parameters, so connectors follow the mesh
5	wherever the targets move it (the MakeHuman "joints follow the mesh" idea).
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
10	import numpy as np
11	
12	from ..geometry.mesh import Mesh
13	from ..geometry.frame import Frame
14	from ..connectors import Connector, PointConnector, PolygonConnector, RectangleConnector, CircleConnector
15	from .generator import RING, RING_N, HALF_N, N_STATIONS, mirror_index, station_index
16	
17	J = RING  # shorthand: J["F"] etc.
18	
19	
20	# ----------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
21	def vidx(mesh: Mesh, station: int, j: int) -> int:
22	    return (station + mesh.meta["ring_offset"]) * RING_N + j
23	
24	
25	def ring_pts(mesh: Mesh, station: int) -> np.ndarray:
26	    a = vidx(mesh, station, 0)
27	    return mesh.vertices[a : a + RING_N]
28	
29	
30	def fit_circle(pts_xz: np.ndarray) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
31	    """Algebraic least-squares circle fit in 2-D -> (cx, cz, r)."""
32	    x, y = pts_xz[:, 0], pts_xz[:, 1]
33	    A = np.column_stack([x, y, np.ones_like(x)])
34	    b = x * x + y * y
35	    sol, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, b, rcond=None)
36	    cx, cy = sol[0] / 2, sol[1] / 2
37	    r = np.sqrt(max(sol[2] + cx * cx + cy * cy, 1e-9))
38	    return float(cx), float(cy), float(r)
39	
40	
41	def surface_line_at_x(mesh: Mesh, x_target: float, j_from: int, j_to: int, stations=None) -> np.ndarray:
42	    """Polyline on the loft surface at constant x, for ring indices j_from..j_to.
43	    Each ring index j is a longitudinal vertex chain; we interpolate along it."""
44	    stations = range(N_STATIONS) if stations is None else stations
45	    out = []
46	    step = 1 if j_to >= j_from else -1
47	    for j in range(j_from, j_to + step, step):
48	        chain = np.array([mesh.vertices[vidx(mesh, i, j)] for i in stations])
49	        xs = chain[:, 0]
50	        k = np.clip(np.searchsorted(xs, x_target) - 1, 0, len(xs) - 2)
51	        t = np.clip((x_target - xs[k]) / max(xs[k + 1] - xs[k], 1e-9), 0, 1)
52	        out.append(chain[k] + (chain[k + 1] - chain[k]) * t)
53	    return np.asarray(out)
54	
55	
56	def aperture_loop(mesh: Mesh, name: str) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Tuple[int, int], np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
57	    """Ordered vertex loop around a grid aperture + (rows, cols) + outward normal
58	    + the full vertex grid (rows, cols, 3) the aperture was cut from."""
59	    r0, r1, j0, j1 = mesh.meta["aperture_rects"][name]
60	    off = mesh.meta["ring_offset"]
61	    # rows are loft ring rows (already include the fascia offset); convert to station space
62	    r0s, r1s = r0 - off, r1 - off + 1
63	    j1e = j1 + 1
64	    loop = []
65	    loop += [vidx(mesh, r, j0) for r in range(r0s, r1s + 1)]
66	    loop += [vidx(mesh, r1s, j) for j in range(j0 + 1, j1e + 1)]
67	    loop += [vidx(mesh, r, j1e) for r in range(r1s - 1, r0s - 1, -1)]
68	    loop += [vidx(mesh, r0s, j) for j in range(j1e - 1, j0, -1)]
69	    pts = mesh.vertices[loop]
70	    grid = np.array([[mesh.vertices[vidx(mesh, r, j)] for j in range(j0, j1e + 1)] for r in range(r0s, r1s + 1)])
71	    faces = mesh.zones[name]
72	    if "_face_normals" not in mesh.meta:
73	        mesh.meta["_face_normals"] = mesh.face_normals()
74	    fn = mesh.meta["_face_normals"][faces].mean(axis=0)
75	    fn /= max(np.linalg.norm(fn), 1e-9)
76	    return pts, (r1s - r0s + 1, j1e - j0 + 1), fn, grid

79	# ------------------------------------------------------------ measurements
80	def measure(mesh: Mesh) -> Dict[str, float]:
81	    V = mesh.vertices
82	    G = mesh.groups
83	
84	    def ring(name):
85	        return V[G[f"ring/{name}"]]
86	
87	    def lring(name):
88	        return V[G[f"lring/{name}"]]
89	
90	    H, E, F, Gj, D, A = J["H"], J["E"], J["F"], J["G"], J["D"], J["A"]
91	    cowl, rf, rr, deck = ring("cowl"), ring("roof_front"), ring("roof_rear"), ring("deck")
92	    bp = ring("bp_r")
93	    m: Dict[str, float] = {}
94	    m["x_front"] = float(V[G["apex_front"]][0, 0])
95	    m["x_rear"] = float(V[G["apex_rear"]][0, 0])
96	    m["length"] = m["x_front"] - m["x_rear"]
97	    m["width"] = float(2 * np.abs(V[:, 1]).max())
98	    m["height"] = float(V[:, 2].max())
99	    m["x_cowl"], m["z_cowl"] = float(cowl[H, 0]), float(cowl[H, 2])
100	    m["x_roof_front"], m["z_roof_front"] = float(rf[H, 0]), float(rf[H, 2])
101	    m["x_roof_rear"], m["z_roof_rear"] = float(rr[H, 0]), float(rr[H, 2])
102	    m["x_deck"], m["z_deck"] = float(deck[H, 0]), float(deck[H, 2])
103	    m["x_bpillar"] = float(0.5 * (ring("bp_r")[Gj, 0] + ring("bp_f")[Gj, 0]))
104	    m["roof_half_width"] = float(0.5 * (rf[Gj, 1] + rr[Gj, 1]))
105	    # cabin section at the B pillar
106	    m["z_belt"] = float(bp[E, 2])
107	    m["y_belt"] = float(bp[E, 1])
108	    m["y_shoulder"] = float(bp[F, 1])
109	    m["z_sill"] = float(np.mean([lring("ra_end")[D, 2], lring("fa_start")[D, 2]]))
110	    m["y_sill"] = float(lring("fa_start")[D, 1])
111	    cabin_st = range(station_index("bp_r") - 4, station_index("bp_f") + 4)
112	    m["z_floor"] = float(np.mean([V[vidx(mesh, i, A), 2] for i in cabin_st]))
113	    m["y_floor_edge"] = float(np.mean([V[vidx(mesh, i, J["B"]), 1] for i in cabin_st]))
114	    # wheels
115	    for tag in ("front", "rear"):
116	        pts = V[G[f"arch_{tag}_L"]][:, [0, 2]]
117	        cx, cz, r = fit_circle(pts)
118	        m[f"wheel_{tag}_x"], m[f"wheel_{tag}_z"], m[f"arch_{tag}_r"] = cx, cz, r
119	        m[f"wheel_{tag}_y"] = float(np.mean(V[G[f"arch_{tag}_L"]][:, 1]))
120	    m["wheelbase"] = m["wheel_front_x"] - m["wheel_rear_x"]
121	    m["track"] = 2 * m["wheel_front_y"]
122	    # nose / tail faces
123	    nose, tail = V[G["nose_ring"]], V[G["tail_ring"]]
124	    m["nose_z_top"], m["nose_z_bottom"] = float(nose[H, 2]), float(nose[A, 2])
125	    m["nose_half_width"] = float(nose[E, 1])
126	    m["nose_top_half_width"] = float(nose[Gj, 1])
127	    m["tail_z_top"], m["tail_z_bottom"] = float(tail[H, 2]), float(tail[A, 2])
128	    m["tail_half_width"] = float(tail[E, 1])
129	    m["tail_top_half_width"] = float(tail[Gj, 1])
130	    m["bed"] = float(max(0.0, V[G["ring/deck"]][H, 2] - V[vidx(mesh, station_index("deck") // 2, H), 2]))
131	    m["has_bed"] = float(m["bed"] > 0.2)
132	    return m

135	# ------------------------------------------------------------ feature lines
136	def feature_lines(mesh: Mesh, meas: Dict[str, float], door_count: int = 4) -> List[Tuple[str, np.ndarray]]:
137	    V = mesh.vertices
138	    lines: List[Tuple[str, np.ndarray]] = []
139	    D, E, F, Gj, H = J["D"], J["E"], J["F"], J["G"], J["H"]
140	    st = station_index
141	    off = mesh.meta["ring_offset"]
142	
143	    def chain(j, i0, i1):
144	        return np.array([V[vidx(mesh, i, j)] for i in range(i0, i1 + 1)])
145	
146	    def ring_seg(i, j0, j1):
147	        r = ring_pts(mesh, i)
148	        idx = list(range(j0, j1 + 1)) if j1 >= j0 else list(range(j0, j1 - 1, -1))
149	        return r[idx]
150	
151	    for side, mir in (("L", lambda j: j), ("R", mirror_index)):
152	        # hood: side seams along the fender/hood edge, rear seam across the cowl
153	        lines.append((f"hood_seam_{side}", chain(mir(F), st("cowl") + 1, st("front") - 3)))
154	        # trunk lid side seams
155	        lines.append((f"deck_seam_{side}", chain(mir(F), 3, st("deck"))))
156	        # B pillar seams sill -> roof rail
157	        for nm in ("bp_r", "bp_f"):
158	            lines.append((f"{nm}_seam_{side}", ring_seg(st(nm), mir(D), mir(Gj))))
159	        # front door leading edge: vertical on the door, then along the A pillar aperture edge
160	        x_fd = meas["wheel_front_x"] - meas["arch_front_r"] - 0.06
161	        vert = surface_line_at_x(mesh, x_fd, mir(D), mir(E))
162	        pil = ring_seg(st("roof_front"), mir(F), mir(Gj))
163	        lines.append((f"front_door_seam_{side}", np.vstack([vert, pil])))
164	        if door_count >= 4:
165	            x_rd = meas["wheel_rear_x"] + meas["arch_rear_r"] + 0.02
166	            vert = surface_line_at_x(mesh, x_rd, mir(D), mir(E))
167	            pil = ring_seg(st("cp_f"), mir(F), mir(Gj))
168	            lines.append((f"rear_door_seam_{side}", np.vstack([vert, pil])))
169	    # transverse seams (over the top)
170	    lines.append(("hood_rear_seam", ring_seg(st("cowl") + 1, F, mirror_index(F))))
171	    lines.append(("deck_front_seam", ring_seg(st("deck"), F, mirror_index(F))))
172	    # nose & tail hood/trunk front edges
173	    lines.append(("hood_front_seam", ring_seg(st("front") - 3, F, mirror_index(F))))
174	    return lines

177	# --------------------------------------------------------------- connectors
178	def emit_connectors(mesh: Mesh, meas: Dict[str, float], hints: Dict) -> List[Connector]:
179	    """All connectors the body emits.  `hints` carries non-geometric options:
180	    door_count, seat_rows ('auto'|int), drive ('left'|'right'), fuel_side."""
181	    V = mesh.vertices
182	    out: List[Connector] = []
183	    door_count = int(hints.get("door_count", 4))
184	    drive = hints.get("drive", "left")
185	    ysign_driver = 1.0 if drive == "left" else -1.0
186	    X, Y, Z = np.eye(3)
187	
188	    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- wheels
189	    tire_w = float(hints.get("tire_width", 0.225))
190	    for tag in ("front", "rear"):
191	        cx, cz, r = meas[f"wheel_{tag}_x"], meas[f"wheel_{tag}_z"], meas[f"arch_{tag}_r"]
192	        tire_r = r - float(hints.get("arch_gap", 0.06))
193	        y = meas[f"wheel_{tag}_y"] - tire_w / 2 - 0.01
194	        for side, ys in (("L", 1.0), ("R", -1.0)):
195	            fr = Frame.from_normal([cx, ys * y, cz], [0, ys, 0], x_hint=X)
196	            out.append(CircleConnector(f"wheel_{tag}_{side}", fr, tire_r, tags=["wheel", f"wheel_{tag}"],
197	                                       meta={"side": "left" if ys > 0 else "right", "axle": tag,
198	                                             "tire_width": tire_w, "arch_radius": r, "steer": tag == "front"}))
199	
200	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- apertures
201	    for name in mesh.meta["aperture_rects"]:
202	        pts, grid, nrm, grid_pts = aperture_loop(mesh, name)
203	        short = name.split("/", 1)[1]
204	        kind = "glass" if short.startswith(("glass", "windshield", "rear_window")) else "light"
205	        tags = [kind, short.rstrip("_LR").rstrip("_")]
206	        if short.startswith("headlight"):
207	            tags.append("headlight")
208	        if short.startswith("taillight"):
209	            tags.append("taillight")
210	        side = "left" if short.endswith("_L") else "right" if short.endswith("_R") else "center"
211	        x_hint = Y if kind == "glass" else X
212	        conn = PolygonConnector.from_points(name.replace("aperture/", ""), pts, normal_hint=nrm, x_hint=x_hint,
213	                                            tags=tags, meta={"grid": list(grid), "grid_points": grid_pts, "side": side, "aperture": True})
214	        out.append(conn)
215	
216	    # --------------------------------------------------------- exterior bits
217	    nose = V[mesh.groups["nose_ring"]]
218	    tail = V[mesh.groups["tail_ring"]]
219	    apex_f = V[mesh.groups["apex_front"]][0]
220	    apex_r = V[mesh.groups["apex_rear"]][0]
221	    nose_n = _face_normal_from_ring(nose, +1)
222	    tail_n = _face_normal_from_ring(tail, -1)
223	    z_nose_top, z_nose_bot = meas["nose_z_top"], meas["nose_z_bottom"]
224	    z_tail_top, z_tail_bot = meas["tail_z_top"], meas["tail_z_bottom"]
225	    nose_w = 2 * meas["nose_top_half_width"]
226	    tail_w = 2 * meas["tail_top_half_width"]
227	
228	    def on_face(apex, nrm, z, ahead=0.004):
229	        # point on the fascia plane at height z (shifted along the normal a bit)
230	        p = np.array([apex[0], 0.0, z])
231	        # move onto the (raked) face: plane through apex with normal nrm
232	        d = np.dot(apex - p, nrm) / max(abs(nrm[0]), 1e-6)
233	        p[0] += d * np.sign(nrm[0])
234	        return p + nrm * ahead
235	
236	    grille_z = z_nose_top - 0.18
237	    out.append(RectangleConnector("grille", Frame.from_normal(on_face(apex_f, nose_n, grille_z), nose_n, x_hint=-Y),
238	                                  min(nose_w * 0.62, 1.1), 0.17, tags=["grille"], meta={"style_hint": hints.get("style", "sedan")}))
239	    intake_z = z_nose_bot + 0.16
240	    out.append(RectangleConnector("intake", Frame.from_normal(on_face(apex_f, nose_n, intake_z), nose_n, x_hint=-Y),
241	                                  min(nose_w * 0.8, 1.2), 0.14, tags=["grille", "intake"], meta={"lower": True}))
242	    plate_z = z_nose_bot + 0.16 + 0.15
243	    out.append(RectangleConnector("plate_front", Frame.from_normal(on_face(apex_f, nose_n, (grille_z + intake_z) / 2 - 0.02, 0.012), nose_n, x_hint=-Y),
244	                                  0.52, 0.11, tags=["plate"], meta={"position": "front"}))
245	    out.append(RectangleConnector("plate_rear", Frame.from_normal(on_face(apex_r, tail_n, z_tail_bot + 0.5 * (z_tail_top - z_tail_bot), 0.012), tail_n, x_hint=Y),
246	                                  0.52, 0.11, tags=["plate"], meta={"position": "rear"}))
247	    out.append(PointConnector("badge_front", Frame.from_normal(on_face(apex_f, nose_n, grille_z + 0.11, 0.012), nose_n, x_hint=-Y), tags=["badge"]))
248	    out.append(PointConnector("badge_rear", Frame.from_normal(on_face(apex_r, tail_n, z_tail_top - 0.16, 0.012), tail_n, x_hint=Y), tags=["badge"]))
249	    # exhaust tips
250	    for side, ys in (("L", 1.0), ("R", -1.0)):
251	        p = on_face(apex_r, tail_n, z_tail_bot + 0.10, 0.0)
252	        p[1] = ys * (meas["tail_half_width"] - 0.32)
253	        out.append(CircleConnector(f"exhaust_{side}", Frame.from_normal(p, tail_n, x_hint=Y), 0.038, tags=["exhaust"],
254	                                   meta={"side": "left" if ys > 0 else "right"}))
255	    # side mirrors at the front-bottom corner of the front door glass
256	    st = station_index
257	    for side, mir, ys in (("L", lambda j: j, 1.0), ("R", mirror_index, -1.0)):
258	        p = V[vidx(mesh, st("roof_front"), mir(J["F"]))].copy()
259	        p[0] += 0.02
260	        p[2] += 0.02
261	        out.append(PointConnector(f"mirror_{side}", Frame.from_normal(p, [0.0, ys, 0.0], x_hint=X), tags=["mirror"],
262	                                  meta={"side": "left" if ys > 0 else "right"}))
263	        # door handles: on the door skin just below the belt, mid-door
264	        x_fd0 = meas["wheel_front_x"] - meas["arch_front_r"] - 0.06
265	        x_fd1 = meas["x_bpillar"]
266	        for door, x0, x1, ok in (("front", x_fd0, x_fd1, True),
267	                                 ("rear", x_fd1, meas["wheel_rear_x"] + meas["arch_rear_r"] + 0.02, door_count >= 4)):
268	            if not ok:
269	                continue
270	            xh = x1 + 0.62 * (x0 - x1)
271	            zh = meas["z_belt"] - 0.11
272	            line = surface_line_at_x(mesh, xh, mir(J["D"]), mir(J["E"]))
273	            k = int(np.argmin(np.abs(line[:, 2] - zh)))
274	            p = line[k].copy()
275	            nrm = np.array([0.0, ys, 0.0])
276	            out.append(PointConnector(f"handle_{door}_{side}", Frame.from_normal(p, nrm, x_hint=X), tags=["handle"],
277	                                      meta={"side": "left" if ys > 0 else "right", "door": door}))
278	        # roof rails along the roof edge (upper chain is numbered rear -> front)
279	        i0, i1 = st("roof_rear") + 1, st("roof_front") - 1
280	        if i1 > i0 + 1:
281	            pts = np.array([V[vidx(mesh, i, mir(J["G"]))] for i in range(i0, i1 + 1)])
282	            length = float(pts[-1, 0] - pts[0, 0])
283	            c = pts.mean(axis=0)
284	            fr = Frame.from_normal(c, Z, x_hint=X)
285	            out.append(RectangleConnector(f"roof_rail_{side}", fr, abs(length), 0.05, tags=["roof_rail"],
286	                                          meta={"side": "left" if ys > 0 else "right", "path": pts}))
287	    # fuel cap on the rear quarter (fuel side from hints)
288	    fs = hints.get("fuel_side", "left")
289	    ys = 1.0 if fs == "left" else -1.0
290	    mir = (lambda j: j) if ys > 0 else mirror_index
291	    xf = meas["wheel_rear_x"] + 0.08
292	    line = surface_line_at_x(mesh, xf, mir(J["D"]), mir(J["E"]))
293	    zf = meas["z_belt"] - 0.20
294	    k = int(np.argmin(np.abs(line[:, 2] - zf)))
295	    out.append(CircleConnector("fuel_cap", Frame.from_normal(line[k], [0, ys, 0], x_hint=X), 0.065, tags=["fuel_cap"],
296	                               meta={"side": fs}))
297	    # antenna / shark fin near the rear of the roof
298	    i_ant = st("roof_rear") + 1
299	    p = V[vidx(mesh, i_ant, J["H"])]
300	    out.append(PointConnector("antenna", Frame.from_normal(p, Z, x_hint=X), tags=["antenna"]))
301	
302	    # -------------------------------------------------------------- interior
303	    out += interior_connectors(mesh, meas, hints)
304	    from .connectors_extra import extra_exterior_connectors
305	    out += extra_exterior_connectors(mesh, meas, hints)
306	    return out

309	def _face_normal_from_ring(ring: np.ndarray, sign: float) -> np.ndarray:
310	    top = ring[J["H"]]
311	    bot = ring[J["A"]]
312	    d = top - bot  # face direction (mostly vertical, tilted by the rake)
313	    n = np.array([d[2], 0.0, -d[0]])
314	    n /= np.linalg.norm(n)
315	    if np.sign(n[0]) != np.sign(sign):
316	        n = -n
317	    return n

320	def interior_connectors(mesh: Mesh, meas: Dict[str, float], hints: Dict) -> List[Connector]:
321	    V = mesh.vertices
322	    out: List[Connector] = []
323	    X, Y, Z = np.eye(3)
324	    door_count = int(hints.get("door_count", 4))
325	    drive = hints.get("drive", "left")
326	    ysd = 1.0 if drive == "left" else -1.0
327	    st = station_index
328	
329	    floor = meas["z_floor"] + 0.05             # cabin floor (carpet top)
330	    inner_half = meas["y_shoulder"] - 0.08     # cabin inner half width at the belt
331	    roof_h = meas["z_roof_front"]
332	    h_point = float(hints.get("h_point_height", np.clip(0.17 + (roof_h - 1.2) * 0.4, 0.17, 0.38)))
333	    x_h1 = meas["x_cowl"] - float(hints.get("front_h_point_offset", 0.95))
334	    z_h1 = floor + h_point
335	    y_seat = min(0.42, inner_half - 0.36)
336	    x_firewall = meas["x_cowl"] + 0.12
337	    has_bed = meas.get("has_bed", 0.0) > 0.5
338	    x_cab_rear = min(meas["x_roof_rear"] - 0.05, meas["x_deck"] + 0.55) if not has_bed else meas["x_deck"] - 0.05
339	    x_cab_rear = min(x_cab_rear, meas["x_roof_rear"] + 0.15)
340	    # seat rows -----------------------------------------------------------------
341	    rows_cfg = hints.get("seat_rows", "auto")
342	    pitch = 0.86
343	    row_x = [x_h1]
344	    while len(row_x) < 3 and row_x[-1] - pitch - 0.30 > x_cab_rear - 0.12:
345	        row_x.append(row_x[-1] - pitch)
346	    if rows_cfg != "auto":
347	        rows_cfg = int(rows_cfg)
348	        row_x = [x_h1 - k * pitch for k in range(max(1, rows_cfg))]
349	    n_rows = len(row_x)
350	    seat_w, seat_d = 0.52, 0.55
351	    for r, xh in enumerate(row_x):
352	        if r == 0:
353	            for name, ys in (("driver", ysd), ("passenger", -ysd)):
354	                fr = Frame.from_normal([xh + 0.12, ys * y_seat, floor], Z, x_hint=X)
355	                out.append(RectangleConnector(f"seat_front_{name}", fr, seat_d, seat_w, tags=["seat", "seat_front"],
356	                                              meta={"row": 0, "role": name, "h_point_height": h_point,
357	                                                    "headroom": roof_h - 0.03 - floor, "side": "left" if ys > 0 else "right"}))
358	        else:
359	            bench_w = 2 * inner_half - 0.12
360	            room = row_x[r - 1] - xh
361	            fr = Frame.from_normal([xh + 0.10, 0.0, floor + (0.02 if r == 1 else 0.0)], Z, x_hint=X)
362	            out.append(RectangleConnector(f"seat_row{r + 1}", fr, seat_d - 0.05, bench_w, tags=["seat", "seat_bench", f"seat_row{r + 1}"],
363	                                          meta={"row": r, "role": "bench", "h_point_height": h_point - 0.02 * r,
364	                                                "headroom": meas["z_roof_rear"] - 0.03 - floor if r == n_rows - 1 else roof_h - floor,
365	                                                "legroom": room}))
366	    # steering wheel / column ---------------------------------------------------
367	    col_angle = np.radians(float(hints.get("column_angle", 24.0)))
368	    wheel_c = np.array([x_h1 + 0.52, ysd * y_seat, z_h1 + 0.32])
369	    n = np.array([-np.cos(col_angle), 0.0, np.sin(col_angle)])
370	    out.append(CircleConnector("steering_wheel", Frame.from_normal(wheel_c, n, x_hint=Y), 0.185, tags=["steering_wheel"],
371	                               meta={"column_angle_deg": float(np.degrees(col_angle)), "column_length": 0.35}))
372	    # dashboard: interior section just behind the windshield base ----------------
373	    cowl = ring_pts(mesh, st("cowl"))
374	    yE = cowl[J["E"], 1] - 0.09
375	    z_top = meas["z_cowl"] - 0.03
376	    z_lo = floor + 0.32
377	    x_dash = meas["x_cowl"] - 0.02
378	    dash_pts = np.array([
379	        [x_dash, -yE, z_lo], [x_dash, yE, z_lo], [x_dash, yE, z_top - 0.12], [x_dash, yE - 0.10, z_top],
380	        [x_dash, -yE + 0.10, z_top], [x_dash, -yE, z_top - 0.12],
381	    ])
382	    dash = PolygonConnector.from_points("dashboard", dash_pts, normal_hint=-X, x_hint=-Y, tags=["dashboard"],
383	                                        meta={"driver_y": ysd * y_seat, "depth": 0.55, "floor": floor,
384	                                              "windshield_x": meas["x_cowl"], "steering_center": wheel_c})
385	    out.append(dash)
386	    # pedals ------------------------------------------------------------------------
387	    out.append(RectangleConnector("pedals", Frame.from_normal([x_h1 + 0.86, ysd * y_seat, floor + 0.02], Z, x_hint=X),
388	                                  0.20, 0.34, tags=["pedals"], meta={"transmission": hints.get("transmission", "automatic")}))
389	    # centre console between the front seats --------------------------------------
390	    console_len = 0.95
391	    out.append(RectangleConnector("console", Frame.from_normal([x_h1 + 0.18, 0.0, floor], Z, x_hint=X), console_len, 0.26,
392	                                  tags=["console"], meta={"height": z_h1 - floor + 0.06, "driver_y": ysd * y_seat}))
393	    # cabin floor --------------------------------------------------------------------
394	    fl_len = x_firewall - x_cab_rear
395	    out.append(RectangleConnector("floor", Frame.from_normal([(x_firewall + x_cab_rear) / 2, 0.0, floor - 0.01], Z, x_hint=X),
396	                                  fl_len, 2 * inner_half + 0.10, tags=["floor"], meta={"tunnel_height": 0.16, "seat_rows": n_rows}))
397	    # firewall / bulkheads (simple rectangles so the cabin reads as enclosed)
398	    out.append(RectangleConnector("firewall", Frame.from_normal([x_firewall, 0.0, (floor + z_lo) / 2], -X, x_hint=-Y),
399	                                  2 * inner_half + 0.10, z_lo - floor + 0.02, tags=["bulkhead"], meta={"position": "front"}))
400	    out.append(RectangleConnector("rear_bulkhead", Frame.from_normal([x_cab_rear, 0.0, (floor + meas["z_belt"]) / 2], X, x_hint=Y),
401	                                  2 * inner_half + 0.10, meas["z_belt"] - floor, tags=["bulkhead"], meta={"position": "rear"}))
402	    # parcel shelf (sedan) or cargo floor (hatch/wagon)
403	    if meas["x_deck"] < x_cab_rear - 0.2 and not has_bed:
404	        length = x_cab_rear - meas["x_deck"]
405	        out.append(RectangleConnector("parcel_shelf", Frame.from_normal([x_cab_rear - length / 2, 0.0, meas["z_deck"] - 0.10], Z, x_hint=X),
406	                                      length, 2 * inner_half + 0.05, tags=["shelf"]))
407	        # trunk floor
408	        tl = length + 0.2
409	        out.append(RectangleConnector("trunk_floor", Frame.from_normal([x_cab_rear - tl / 2 - 0.05, 0.0, floor + 0.10], Z, x_hint=X),

1	"""Connectors: typed attachment sites emitted by the body (and by components).
2	
3	Hierarchy (a component that accepts a base type accepts all subtypes):
4	
5	    Connector
6	     ├── PointConnector                 a location + orientation
7	     └── PolygonConnector               a closed 3-D outline (roughly planar)
8	          ├── RectangleConnector        width x height in the frame's XY plane
9	          └── CircleConnector           radius in the frame's XY plane
10	
11	Every connector carries a `Frame` whose Z axis is the mount normal (things are
12	built along +Z in local space) and whose X axis is the connector's major
13	direction (car-forward for most interior parts, lateral for windows).
14	`tags` are used by the config to select which component goes where, and `meta`
15	carries free-form hints (e.g. tire width, seat row, driver side).
16	"""
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
20	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple
21	import numpy as np
22	
23	from .geometry.frame import Frame
24	from .geometry.curves import circle_points, polygon_area_2d, polygon_centroid_2d
25	
26	
27	class Connector:
28	    kind = "connector"
29	
30	    def __init__(self, name: str, frame: Frame, tags: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None, meta: Optional[dict] = None,
31	                 owner: str = "body"):
32	        self.name = name
33	        self.frame = frame
34	        self.tags: Set[str] = set(tags or [])
35	        self.meta: Dict[str, Any] = dict(meta or {})
36	        self.owner = owner  # who emitted it ("body" or a component instance name)
37	
38	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ geometry
39	    @property
40	    def origin(self) -> np.ndarray:
41	        return self.frame.origin
42	
43	    @property
44	    def normal(self) -> np.ndarray:
45	        return self.frame.z_axis
46	
47	    def side(self) -> str:
48	        return self.meta.get("side", "left" if self.origin[1] > 0.01 else "right" if self.origin[1] < -0.01 else "center")
49	
50	    # ----------------------------------------------------------- matching
51	    def matches(self, selector: str) -> bool:
52	        """Selector grammar: exact name, tag, or glob on the name ('seat.*')."""
53	        import fnmatch
54	
55	        if selector == self.name or selector in self.tags:
56	            return True
57	        return fnmatch.fnmatchcase(self.name, selector)
58	
59	    @classmethod
60	    def accepts(cls, other_cls: type) -> bool:
61	        return issubclass(other_cls, cls)
62	
63	    # ---------------------------------------------------------- serialise
64	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
65	        return {
66	            "name": self.name,
67	            "kind": self.kind,
68	            "owner": self.owner,
69	            "tags": sorted(self.tags),
70	            "frame": self.frame.to_dict(),
71	            "meta": {k: _jsonable(v) for k, v in self.meta.items() if k != "grid_points"},
72	        }
73	
74	    def mirrored(self, new_name: str) -> "Connector":
75	        c = self.__class__.__new__(self.__class__)
76	        c.__dict__.update(self.__dict__)
77	        c.name = new_name
78	        c.frame = self.frame.mirrored_y()
79	        c.tags = set(self.tags)
80	        c.meta = dict(self.meta)
81	        c.meta["side"] = "right" if self.meta.get("side") == "left" else "left" if self.meta.get("side") == "right" else self.meta.get("side")
82	        return c
83	
84	    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover
85	        return f"{self.__class__.__name__}({self.name!r}, origin={np.round(self.origin, 3).tolist()})"
86	
87	
88	class PointConnector(Connector):
89	    kind = "point"
90	
91	
92	class PolygonConnector(Connector):
93	    """Closed outline in 3-D.  Points are stored in world space; `local_points`
94	    projects them onto the frame's XY plane."""
95	
96	    kind = "polygon"
97	
98	    def __init__(self, name: str, frame: Frame, points_world: np.ndarray, tags=None, meta=None, owner="body"):
99	        super().__init__(name, frame, tags, meta, owner)
100	        self._points = np.asarray(points_world, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 3)
101	
102	    @classmethod
103	    def from_points(cls, name: str, points_world, normal_hint=None, x_hint=None, tags=None, meta=None, owner="body"):
104	        """Build a polygon connector with a best-fit plane frame from 3-D points."""
105	        pts = np.asarray(points_world, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 3)
106	        c = pts.mean(axis=0)
107	        # Newell normal
108	        nrm = np.zeros(3)
109	        for i in range(len(pts)):
110	            a, b = pts[i], pts[(i + 1) % len(pts)]
111	            nrm += np.cross(a, b)
112	        if np.linalg.norm(nrm) < 1e-9:
113	            nrm = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
114	        nrm /= np.linalg.norm(nrm)
115	        meta = dict(meta or {})
116	        if normal_hint is not None:
117	            hint = np.asarray(normal_hint, dtype=float)
118	            hint /= np.linalg.norm(hint)
119	            if np.dot(nrm, hint) < 0:
120	                # reverse the winding; a grid loop (side0=rows, side1=cols, ...) stays a valid grid loop
121	                # if we restart at the same corner, which swaps the roles of rows and cols
122	                nrm = -nrm
123	                pts = np.roll(pts[::-1], 1, axis=0)
124	                if meta.get("grid"):
125	                    rows, cols = meta["grid"]
126	                    meta["grid"] = [int(cols), int(rows)]
127	                if meta.get("grid_points") is not None:
128	                    meta["grid_points"] = np.asarray(meta["grid_points"]).transpose(1, 0, 2).copy()
129	            # for strongly non-planar outlines (wrap-around lamps) the hint, e.g. the mean
130	            # surface normal of the aperture, is the better mount normal than the Newell fit
131	            if np.dot(nrm, hint) < np.cos(np.radians(25.0)):
132	                nrm = hint
133	        if x_hint is None:
134	            # major axis via PCA in the plane
135	            q = pts - c
136	            q = q - np.outer(q @ nrm, nrm)
137	            u, s, vt = np.linalg.svd(q, full_matrices=False)
138	            x_hint = vt[0]
139	        frame = Frame.from_normal(c, nrm, x_hint)
140	        return cls(name, frame, pts, tags, meta, owner)
141	
142	    @property
143	    def points(self) -> np.ndarray:
144	        return self._points
145	
146	    def local_points(self) -> np.ndarray:
147	        return self.frame.to_local(self._points)[:, :2]
148	
149	    @property
150	    def area(self) -> float:
151	        return abs(polygon_area_2d(self.local_points()))
152	
153	    @property
154	    def centroid(self) -> np.ndarray:
155	        c2 = polygon_centroid_2d(self.local_points())
156	        return self.frame.to_world([[c2[0], c2[1], 0.0]])[0]
157	
158	    def extents(self) -> Tuple[float, float]:
159	        lp = self.local_points()
160	        return float(np.ptp(lp[:, 0])), float(np.ptp(lp[:, 1]))
161	
162	    @property
163	    def width(self) -> float:
164	        return self.extents()[0]
165	
166	    @property
167	    def height(self) -> float:
168	        return self.extents()[1]
169	
170	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
171	        d = super().to_dict()
172	        d["points"] = np.round(self._points, 4).tolist()
173	        d["width"] = round(self.width, 4)
174	        d["height"] = round(self.height, 4)
175	        d["area"] = round(self.area, 4)
176	        return d
177	
178	    def mirrored(self, new_name: str) -> "PolygonConnector":
179	        c = super().mirrored(new_name)
180	        pts = self._points * np.array([1.0, -1.0, 1.0])
181	        c._points = pts[::-1].copy()
182	        return c  # type: ignore
183	
184	
185	class RectangleConnector(PolygonConnector):
186	    kind = "rectangle"
187	
188	    def __init__(self, name: str, frame: Frame, width: float, height: float, tags=None, meta=None, owner="body"):
189	        hw, hh = width / 2.0, height / 2.0
190	        local = np.array([[-hw, -hh, 0], [hw, -hh, 0], [hw, hh, 0], [-hw, hh, 0]], dtype=float)
191	        super().__init__(name, frame, frame.to_world(local), tags, meta, owner)
192	        self._width = float(width)
193	        self._height = float(height)
194	
195	    @property
196	    def width(self) -> float:
197	        return self._width
198	
199	    @property
200	    def height(self) -> float:
201	        return self._height
202	
203	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
204	        d = super().to_dict()
205	        d["width"], d["height"] = round(self._width, 4), round(self._height, 4)
206	        return d
207	
208	
209	class CircleConnector(PolygonConnector):
210	    kind = "circle"
211	
212	    def __init__(self, name: str, frame: Frame, radius: float, tags=None, meta=None, owner="body", segments: int = 32):
213	        c2 = circle_points(radius, segments)
214	        local = np.hstack([c2, np.zeros((segments, 1))])
215	        super().__init__(name, frame, frame.to_world(local), tags, meta, owner)
216	        self.radius = float(radius)
217	
218	    @property
219	    def diameter(self) -> float:
220	        return 2 * self.radius
221	
222	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
223	        d = super().to_dict()
224	        d["radius"] = round(self.radius, 4)
225	        return d
226	
227	
228	def _jsonable(v):
229	    if isinstance(v, np.ndarray):
230	        return np.round(v, 5).tolist()
231	    if isinstance(v, (np.floating,)):
232	        return float(v)
233	    if isinstance(v, (np.integer,)):
234	        return int(v)
235	    return v
236	
237	
238	CONNECTOR_TYPES = {
239	    "point": PointConnector,
240	    "polygon": PolygonConnector,
241	    "rectangle": RectangleConnector,
242	    "circle": CircleConnector,
243	}

1	"""Right-handed coordinate frames used to place connectors and components.
2	
3	Car convention (world): +X forward, +Y left, +Z up, ground at Z = 0.
4	
5	A Frame has an origin and three orthonormal axes.  By convention the frame's
6	Z axis is the *mount normal* of a connector (the direction things stick out
7	along) and its X axis is the connector's "major" direction.
8	"""
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
12	import numpy as np
13	
14	_EPS = 1e-9
15	
16	
17	def unit(v: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
18	    v = np.asarray(v, dtype=float)
19	    n = np.linalg.norm(v)
20	    if n < _EPS:
21	        raise ValueError("cannot normalise a zero vector")
22	    return v / n
23	
24	
25	@dataclass
26	class Frame:
27	    origin: np.ndarray = field(default_factory=lambda: np.zeros(3))
28	    x_axis: np.ndarray = field(default_factory=lambda: np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0]))
29	    y_axis: np.ndarray = field(default_factory=lambda: np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]))
30	    z_axis: np.ndarray = field(default_factory=lambda: np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]))
31	
32	    def __post_init__(self):
33	        self.origin = np.asarray(self.origin, dtype=float).reshape(3)
34	        self.x_axis = unit(self.x_axis)
35	        self.y_axis = unit(self.y_axis)
36	        self.z_axis = unit(self.z_axis)
37	
38	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ builders
39	    @classmethod
40	    def identity(cls, origin=(0, 0, 0)) -> "Frame":
41	        return cls(np.asarray(origin, dtype=float))
42	
43	    @classmethod
44	    def from_normal(cls, origin, normal, x_hint=(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)) -> "Frame":
45	        """Frame whose Z axis is `normal`; X is `x_hint` projected onto the plane."""
46	        z = unit(normal)
47	        hint = np.asarray(x_hint, dtype=float)
48	        x = hint - np.dot(hint, z) * z
49	        if np.linalg.norm(x) < 1e-6:
50	            # hint parallel to the normal: pick any perpendicular direction
51	            alt = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]) if abs(z[2]) < 0.9 else np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
52	            x = alt - np.dot(alt, z) * z
53	        x = unit(x)
54	        y = np.cross(z, x)
55	        return cls(np.asarray(origin, dtype=float), x, y, z)
56	
57	    @classmethod
58	    def from_axes(cls, origin, x_axis, z_axis) -> "Frame":
59	        z = unit(z_axis)
60	        x = np.asarray(x_axis, dtype=float)
61	        x = unit(x - np.dot(x, z) * z)
62	        return cls(np.asarray(origin, dtype=float), x, np.cross(z, x), z)
63	
64	    # -------------------------------------------------------------- conversions
65	    @property
66	    def rotation(self) -> np.ndarray:
67	        """3x3 matrix whose columns are the axes (local -> world rotation)."""
68	        return np.stack([self.x_axis, self.y_axis, self.z_axis], axis=1)
69	
70	    @property
71	    def matrix(self) -> np.ndarray:
72	        m = np.eye(4)
73	        m[:3, :3] = self.rotation
74	        m[:3, 3] = self.origin
75	        return m
76	
77	    def to_world(self, pts) -> np.ndarray:
78	        p = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(pts, dtype=float))
79	        return p @ self.rotation.T + self.origin
80	
81	    def to_local(self, pts) -> np.ndarray:
82	        p = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(pts, dtype=float))
83	        return (p - self.origin) @ self.rotation
84	
85	    def dir_to_world(self, v) -> np.ndarray:
86	        return np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(v, dtype=float)) @ self.rotation.T
87	
88	    def transformed(self, m4: np.ndarray) -> "Frame":
89	        r = m4[:3, :3]
90	        return Frame(r @ self.origin + m4[:3, 3], r @ self.x_axis, r @ self.y_axis, r @ self.z_axis)
91	
92	    def translated(self, d) -> "Frame":
93	        return Frame(self.origin + np.asarray(d, dtype=float), self.x_axis, self.y_axis, self.z_axis)
94	
95	    def offset_local(self, dx=0.0, dy=0.0, dz=0.0) -> "Frame":
96	        return self.translated(dx * self.x_axis + dy * self.y_axis + dz * self.z_axis)
97	
98	    def rotated_about_z(self, angle: float) -> "Frame":
99	        c, s = np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)
100	        x = c * self.x_axis + s * self.y_axis
101	        return Frame(self.origin.copy(), x, np.cross(self.z_axis, x), self.z_axis.copy())
102	
103	    def rotated_about_x(self, angle: float) -> "Frame":
104	        c, s = np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)
105	        z = c * self.z_axis + s * self.y_axis
106	        return Frame(self.origin.copy(), self.x_axis.copy(), np.cross(z, self.x_axis), z)
107	
108	    def rotated_about_y(self, angle: float) -> "Frame":
109	        c, s = np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)
110	        z = c * self.z_axis - s * self.x_axis
111	        x = np.cross(self.y_axis, z)
112	        return Frame(self.origin.copy(), x, self.y_axis.copy(), z)
113	
114	    def mirrored_y(self) -> "Frame":
115	        """Mirror across the car's centre plane (Y -> -Y) keeping right-handedness."""
116	        m = np.diag([1.0, -1.0, 1.0])
117	        o = m @ self.origin
118	        x = m @ self.x_axis
119	        z = m @ self.z_axis
120	        return Frame(o, x, np.cross(z, x), z)
121	
122	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
123	        return {
124	            "origin": [round(float(v), 5) for v in self.origin],
125	            "x_axis": [round(float(v), 5) for v in self.x_axis],
126	            "y_axis": [round(float(v), 5) for v in self.y_axis],
127	            "z_axis": [round(float(v), 5) for v in self.z_axis],
128	        }
129	
130	    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover
131	        o = ", ".join(f"{v:.3f}" for v in self.origin)
132	        z = ", ".join(f"{v:.2f}" for v in self.z_axis)
133	        return f"Frame(origin=({o}), normal=({z}))"
134	
135	
136	def rotation_matrix(axis, angle: float) -> np.ndarray:
137	    """4x4 rotation about an arbitrary axis through the origin."""
138	    a = unit(axis)
139	    c, s = np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)
140	    x, y, z = a
141	    r = np.array(
142	        [
143	            [c + x * x * (1 - c), x * y * (1 - c) - z * s, x * z * (1 - c) + y * s],
144	            [y * x * (1 - c) + z * s, c + y * y * (1 - c), y * z * (1 - c) - x * s],
145	            [z * x * (1 - c) - y * s, z * y * (1 - c) + x * s, c + z * z * (1 - c)],
146	        ]
147	    )
148	    m = np.eye(4)
149	    m[:3, :3] = r
150	    return m
151	
152	
153	def translation_matrix(d) -> np.ndarray:
154	    m = np.eye(4)
155	    m[:3, 3] = np.asarray(d, dtype=float)
156	    return m
157	
158	
159	def scale_matrix(sx, sy=None, sz=None) -> np.ndarray:
160	    if sy is None:
161	        sy = sx
162	    if sz is None:
163	        sz = sx
164	    return np.diag([sx, sy, sz, 1.0])

1	"""Component framework.
2	
3	A `CarComponent` attaches to a `Connector` and produces a mesh (plus optional
4	sub-connectors of its own, so that e.g. a dashboard can offer gauge-cluster and
5	vent connectors to further components).
6	
7	Type matching uses the connector class hierarchy: a component that `accepts`
8	`PolygonConnector` also accepts `RectangleConnector` and `CircleConnector`.
9	
10	`MorphableComponent` is the target-based flavour and uses *exactly* the same
11	machinery as the body: a fixed-topology parametric generator, a set of
12	`ModifierSpec`s turned into differential targets, and a `fit()` step that maps
13	the connector's geometry (radius, width, height, meta hints) onto modifier
14	values in [-1, 1].
15	
16	Local frame convention for all components: build in the connector's local
17	frame where +Z is the mount normal (things grow along +Z), +X the connector's
18	major direction, origin at the connector origin.  `build()` transforms the
19	result into world space.
20	"""
21	from __future__ import annotations
22

76	class CarComponent:
77	    """Base class: procedural component bound to a connector type."""
78	
79	    name: str = "component"
80	    accepts: Tuple[Type[Connector], ...] = (Connector,)
81	    default_for: Tuple[str, ...] = ()       # connector tags this is the default for
82	    priority: int = 0                       # higher wins among defaults for the same tag
83	    options: Dict[str, Any] = {}            # documented defaults
84	    description: str = ""
85	
86	    @classmethod
87	    def can_attach(cls, connector: Connector) -> bool:
88	        return isinstance(connector, cls.accepts)
89	
90	    def resolve_options(self, options: Optional[dict]) -> dict:
91	        o = dict(self.options)
92	        o.update(options or {})
93	        return o
94	
95	    def build(self, connector: Connector, options: Optional[dict], ctx: BuildContext) -> ComponentResult:
96	        if not self.can_attach(connector):
97	            raise TypeError(f"{self.name} accepts {[t.__name__ for t in self.accepts]}, got {type(connector).__name__} ({connector.name})")
98	        opts = self.resolve_options(options)
99	        result = self.build_local(connector, opts, ctx)
100	        result.mesh.apply_frame(connector.frame)
101	        result.mesh.name = f"{connector.name}:{self.name}"
102	        for c in result.connectors:
103	            c.frame = c.frame.transformed(connector.frame.matrix)
104	            if isinstance(c, PolygonConnector):
105	                c._points = connector.frame.to_world(c._points)
106	            c.owner = connector.name
107	            c.name = f"{connector.name}/{c.name}"
108	        return result

110	    # subclasses implement this in the connector's local frame
111	    def build_local(self, connector: Connector, opts: dict, ctx: BuildContext) -> ComponentResult:
112	        raise NotImplementedError
113	
114	    @classmethod
115	    def describe(cls) -> dict:
116	        return {
117	            "name": cls.name,
118	            "accepts": [t.__name__ for t in cls.accepts],
119	            "default_for": list(cls.default_for),
120	            "options": dict(cls.options),
121	            "description": cls.description,
122	            "morphable": issubclass(cls, MorphableComponent),
123	        }

126	class MorphableComponent(CarComponent):
127	    """Target-based component (same logic as the body).
128	
129	    Subclasses define:
130	      params_cls        dataclass of generator parameters (canonical values)
131	      modifier_specs    list[ModifierSpec] -> differential targets
132	      generate(params)  fixed-topology mesh in the local frame
133	      fit(connector, opts, ctx) -> {modifier: value in [-1,1]}
134	      sub_connectors(connector, opts, ctx, values) -> local-frame connectors
135	    Variant generators (e.g. bench vs bucket seat) can be exposed as *macro*
136	    targets by overriding `macros()`.
137	    """
138	
139	    params_cls: Type = None  # type: ignore
140	    modifier_specs: List[ModifierSpec] = []
141	    _libraries: Dict[str, MorphableMesh] = {}
142	
143	    def canonical(self):
144	        return self.params_cls()
145	
146	    def macros(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
147	        return {}
148	
149	    def generate(self, params) -> Mesh:
150	        raise NotImplementedError
151	
152	    def fit(self, connector: Connector, opts: dict, ctx: BuildContext) -> Dict[str, float]:
153	        return {}
154	
155	    def sub_connectors(self, connector: Connector, opts: dict, ctx: BuildContext, values: Dict[str, float]) -> List[Connector]:
156	        return []
157	
158	    def library(self) -> MorphableMesh:
159	        key = f"{type(self).__module__}.{type(self).__name__}"
160	        lib = MorphableComponent._libraries.get(key)
161	        if lib is None:
162	            builder = DifferentialTargetBuilder(self.generate, self.canonical(), name=self.name)
163	            lib = builder.build(self.modifier_specs, macros=self.macros(), macro_group="variant")
164	            MorphableComponent._libraries[key] = lib
165	        return lib
166	
167	    @staticmethod
168	    def ratio_to_value(actual: float, canonical: float, delta_minus: float, delta_plus: float) -> float:
169	        """Map a desired physical value onto a bipolar slider value (clamped)."""
170	        d = actual - canonical
171	        if d >= 0:
172	            return float(np.clip(d / delta_plus, 0, 1)) if delta_plus else 0.0
173	        return float(np.clip(d / delta_minus, -1, 0)) if delta_minus else 0.0
174	
175	    def spec(self, name: str) -> ModifierSpec:
176	        for s in self.modifier_specs:
177	            if (s.name or s.param) == name:
178	                return s
179	        raise KeyError(name)
180	
181	    def value_for(self, name: str, actual: float) -> float:
182	        s = self.spec(name)
183	        canon = getattr(self.canonical(), s.param)
184	        return self.ratio_to_value(actual, canon, s.delta_minus, s.delta_plus)
185	
186	    def materials(self, ctx: BuildContext, opts: dict) -> Dict[str, Material]:
187	        return {}
188	
189	    def build_local(self, connector: Connector, opts: dict, ctx: BuildContext) -> ComponentResult:
190	        values = self.fit(connector, opts, ctx)
191	        lib = self.library()
192	        for k in list(values):
193	            if k not in lib.modifiers:
194	                raise KeyError(f"{self.name}: fit() produced unknown modifier {k!r}")
195	        mesh = lib.morph(values)
196	        mesh.materials.update(self.materials(ctx, opts))
197	        subs = self.sub_connectors(connector, opts, ctx, values)
198	        return ComponentResult(mesh, subs, {"modifier_values": values})
199	
200	
201	# ------------------------------------------------------------------- registry
202	REGISTRY: Dict[str, Type[CarComponent]] = {}
203	
204	
205	def register(cls: Type[CarComponent]) -> Type[CarComponent]:
206	    if not cls.name or cls.name in REGISTRY:
207	        raise ValueError(f"component name missing or duplicate: {cls.name!r}")
208	    REGISTRY[cls.name] = cls
209	    return cls
210	
211	
212	def get_component(name: str) -> CarComponent:
213	    if name not in REGISTRY:
214	        raise KeyError(f"unknown component {name!r}; available: {sorted(REGISTRY)}")
215	    return REGISTRY[name]()
216	
217	
218	def default_component_for(connector: Connector) -> Optional[str]:
219	    """Pick the default component for a connector by its tags (then by type)."""
220	    best: Tuple[int, str] | None = None
221	    for name, cls in REGISTRY.items():
222	        if not cls.can_attach(connector):
223	            continue
224	        for tag in cls.default_for:
225	            if tag in connector.tags or tag == connector.name:
226	                score = cls.priority * 10 + (5 if tag == connector.name else 0)
227	                if best is None or score > best[0]:
228	                    best = (score, name)
229	    return best[1] if best else None
230	
231	
232	def describe_all() -> List[dict]:
233	    return [cls.describe() for cls in REGISTRY.values()]
